art.title: Still Life with Flowers in a Glass Vase
art.credit: Public domain · image via Wikimedia Commons (Rijksmuseum)
art.story: An iris, a poppy, an orange marigold and pink roses burst out of a glass vase on a stone ledge, glowing against the darkness, with buds still waiting to open. Look closer and the bouquet is alive: insects crawl and settle among the leaves and petals. These flowers never bloomed at the same time; Rachel Ruysch put them together from studies made over many seasons. Daughter of a famous scientist, she painted for nearly seventy years, raised ten children, and was paid more for her work than Rembrandt was for his.
